summary: Registering a GitHub OAuth app is self-serve, with no provider review or payment, so any GitHub account can connect right away. The main thing that can hold up launch is organization approval: members of an org with OAuth app access restrictions cannot authorize your app until that org's owner approves it.
timeToProduction: Same day for personal-account users. Members of restricted organizations wait for their org owner to approve the app, and the owner controls that timing.

gates.title: Any GitHub account can register the app
No test mode with user caps
No provider review before users can connect
Organizations must approve your app before their members can connect
gates.what: If an org has OAuth app access restrictions on, its members and outside collaborators must request approval from an owner before they can authorize your app. Until approved, your app can only reach the org's public resources. New orgs have restrictions on by default.
gates.where: Organization settings, Third-party Access, OAuth app policy. The org owner acts here, not you.
gates.todo: Tell target organizations' owners to approve the app. Members can request approval from the app's authorization flow, and owners are notified.

gates.title: No paid plan needed for production API access
No recurring re-verification, but GitHub can cut off access at its discretion

requirements.text: A GitHub account. Register the app under your personal account or under an organization where you are an admin.
A public homepage URL for the app, entered as the full URL in the registration form.
Only public information in the app's name, homepage and description, since these are visible to users.

steps.text: Open Settings, then Developer settings, then OAuth Apps, then New OAuth App.
steps.detail: The button reads 'Register a new application' if this is your first app.

steps.text: Enter the application name, homepage URL, optional description and authorization callback URL.
steps.detail: Keep internal URLs out of these fields. Add more callback URLs only if you need them (up to 10).

steps.text: Decide whether to enable the device flow, and whether to keep 'Expire user access tokens' on.
steps.detail: Token expiry is on by default. Turn it off only if your app does not yet support short-lived tokens.

steps.text: Click Register application, then store the client secret on the server.
steps.detail: Never put the client secret in client-side code or on a user device.

steps.text: Connect your own GitHub account to confirm the flow works end to end.
steps.detail: Your personal account needs a verified email address before it can authorize any OAuth app.

steps.text: Ask each target organization's owner to approve the app.
steps.detail: Owners review the app under OAuth app policy and click Grant access.

steps.text: Launch to users with personal accounts, and to org members once their org has approved the app.
steps.detail: Org members who are not yet approved can still use the app with their personal account.

blockers.problem: Org members see an error or cannot authorize the app.
blockers.fix: The org has OAuth app access restrictions on and has not approved the app. Members must request approval, and the org owner must grant access.

blockers.problem: Users cannot authorize the app because their email is unverified.
blockers.fix: The user must verify their email address on GitHub before authorizing any OAuth app.

blockers.problem: Short-lived tokens break the app's sign-in after registration.
blockers.fix: Default token expiry is on. Either update the app to handle expiring tokens or turn the option off until it does.

blockers.problem: The client secret is exposed in a browser or mobile build.
blockers.fix: Keep the client secret on the server only. Rotate it if it was exposed.

blockers.problem: GitHub cuts off your app without notice.
blockers.fix: GitHub may change or end API access at any time. Monitor the Registered Developer Agreement and the app's status, and plan a fallback path.

couldNotVerify: Whether the GitHub Marketplace listing path has its own review rules. Not checked.
